LESSON: TOPOGRAPHICAL MAPS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.1: Topographical maps
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Topographical maps, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: howing human activities, Why are topographical maps important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Topographical maps together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: learners use digital or print resources to find out how human activities are represented in topographical

maps.

• Learning to Learn: learners brainstorm on human activities that may be represented in a topographical map.

Values:
• Integrity: learners display honesty while sharing available resources for drawing sketch maps to enlarge and reduce part of

topographical maps and present to peers.

• Love: learners share resources as they draw sketch maps to enlarge and reduce part of topographical maps and present

them to peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Self-esteem: learners demonstrate the capacity to draw cross-sections from topographical maps showing human activities.

• Peer education: learners display the cross-sections and take a gallery walk and peer assess.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Learners apply Creative Arts skills to draw sketch maps to enlarge and reduce part of topographical maps and present

them to peers.

• Learners use Mathematics knowledge to draw cross-sections from topographical maps showing human activities.
